Side projects: dashboards, tooling, and the occasional over-engineered solution to a problem nobody asked me to solve. Everything is built in R unless noted, and everything is open, so you can see exactly how over-engineered.

::: {.project}
<h3>Presumptive Laws Dashboard</h3><span class="tag tag--wip">under construction</span>

A state-by-state history of first responder presumptive workers' compensation laws: which conditions get presumed work-related, for whom, and since when. Every claim is traced to the statute itself, not to somebody's summary of it. Fifty scattered laws in one place, so nobody else has to do what I did to build it.

<div class="stack">R · Quarto · Shiny <a href="https://github.com/ALERRT-Research/PROJ_presumptive_laws">{{< fa brands github >}} source</a></div>
:::

::: {.project}
<h3>anatomogramdata</h3><span class="tag">R package</span>

Human body maps as tidy polygon data, ready for ggplot2. The outlines are parsed straight from the EBI Expression Atlas anatomogram source files, not copied from a frozen snapshot, and every organ carries its ontology ID and organ system, male and female. It is a data package on purpose: no custom geom and no plotting function, just polygons you plot with the ggplot2 you already know.

<div class="stack">R · ggplot2 <a href="https://petertanksley.github.io/anatomogramdata/">{{< fa book >}} docs</a><a href="https://github.com/petertanksley/anatomogramdata">{{< fa brands github >}} source</a></div>
:::
